head: chevalier_louis_p

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_letter_list names this person at Chicago by 20 May 1835 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1835-05-20 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1835.

origin.value: The French colonial settlements of the Detroit and Milwaukee country
origin.note: ARGUED FROM THE NAME, AND A SURNAME IS NOT A NATIONALITY. This household's surname is carried by the french_colonial pool in data/reconstruction/1835_invented_name_pools.json and by no other pool, and that pool's `evidence` field states what this dataset attests about who bore those names in this town. The French colonial value names a COUNTRY OF ORIGIN and no community membership. The pool it comes from is labelled 'French colonial and metis'; saying of anybody in this town that they were Metis or Native is stage `underdocumented`'s (T-1177) alone, under the standing Indigenous-history constraint AGENTS.md sets, and is not said here.

basis.note: The one community pool that carries this surname points at an origin more sharply than a draw over a roll of seventy births does.

reason_for_coming.value: The 1833 season: the harbour appropriation, the treaty at Chicago and the first rush of settlers
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THE SEASON AND NOTHING ELSE. No trade is recorded for this household and no source says why it came; the only thing the evidence gives is when it was here by. This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.cohort_reasons — the household's arrival year (1833) is the only thing about it this value rests on.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded here, so there is no premises to seek; T-0633 is where a later directory's address gets back-projected.

last_dated_appearance.note: A DATED READING OF THIS PERSON, AND THE LAST ONE THE CORPUS HOLDS. Read from `church_evidence` as `1835-06-06`, which reaches 1835-06-06 — 25 day(s) short of 1835-07-01. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source in this pass's evidence records an occupation for this person. A poll list, a tax list, a muster roll and a baptismal entry each print a name and no trade, and where a later directory prints one it is a trade of 1843 — T-0633 is the rule for back-projecting that, and this pass does not have it.

THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'chevalier_louis_p:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 15 under 20', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('chevalier_louis_p:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'Louis P.' against 'Louis P.' — the forename AND the middle initial agree on every printing, so nothing but one doubled L in a nine-letter French surname stands between the cards. Neither stem is otherwise populated by this pair's bearer: the town holds one Chevallier of this forename and one Chevalier of it. Both readings are the Chicago Democrat inside the window.
merge_ruling.against_merge: ONE CORPUS ID, TWO PRINTINGS SIXTEEN MONTHS APART, AND NEITHER SETS BOTH. Both cards cite `chicago_newspapers_1833_1835`, so a grep over the corpus finds both spellings — but that id is three years of two papers, and the printings are identified: 'Louis P. Chevallier' is the Democrat of 21 January 1834 (#c006) and 'Louis P. Chevalier' the Democrat of 20 May 1835 (#c013). No single issue is caught setting both spellings for one man, so C9's demonstration is absent; no roll enters both as separate entries either, so D5 is unavailable; and because both cards cite one source id, D7's 'the two bodies of evidence do not touch' is literally false and that refusal is not available as written. This is the gap D9 exists to close, measured at the PRINTING rather than at the source id. Neither card is an anchor. The Chevalier side carries a third reading — 'L. Chevalier', a witness in St Mary's on 6 June 1835 — which the Chevallier side has nothing to meet. D9.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.
